transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, lately, after I get off a long shift at the shop, I just... I end up eating way more than I plan to. Like, I'll grab a full fast-food meal on the way home, and then... I don't know, just keep going with whatever snacks or stuff is left in the fridge. Just all in one sitting. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
How often do you find yourself eating a significantly larger amount of food than most people would in a similar period of time, and under similar circumstances?

Um... I guess it happens... maybe once a week? Sometimes more. It's been like that for... a few months, I think. But, you know, after I do that, I... I feel like I have to fix it. So I might... throw up, or take something, or just not eat the next day. Or hit the gym really hard. Just... to balance it out, I guess.
When you're eating this large amount of food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah... I guess. Um... once I start on those nights, it's... it's like my hands just keep grabbing food. Even if I'm, you know, telling myself to stop. Or if I'm already feeling sick. I just... yeah, I can't really quit.
How long does one of these episodes usually last? Like, from the time you start eating until it feels like it's over?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't exactly look at the clock when it's happening. Just... however long it takes until I feel sick, I guess. I've never really timed it.
After these eating episodes, do you regularly make yourself vomit, use laxatives, diuretics, or enemas, or fast or exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?

Yeah... um, like I said before. Sometimes I just... go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or I'll take some laxatives. I just... I get kind of freaked out about what all that food is gonna do to me. So, yeah. I do that.
Can you estimate how long these eating episodes typically last, from start to finish, in minutes or hours?
I don't know... I really don't. Like I said, I don't look at a clock. Maybe an hour? Or two? I just... I don't pay attention to the time.
During these eating episodes, does the eating feel out of control, like you couldn't stop even if you wanted to, and do they happen in a single, limited time period, like within a couple of hours?

Yeah, I guess. It's... it's like I can't stop. Once I start, my hands just keep grabbing stuff. Even when I'm telling myself to quit, and my stomach already hurts. It just happens. And yeah, it's usually all at once... like in that hour or two I mentioned.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets criteria for recurrent episodes of binge eating with loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative use, fasting, excessive exercise). The pattern aligns with bulimia nervosa (F50.2). No evidence of anorexia nervosa (F50.0) or binge eating disorder (F50.1) was found.
